newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CHH says MDF, pulp prices were soft.
newsitem.headline: CHH says MDF, pulp prices were soft.

text.p: Carter Holt Harvey Ltd said on Tuesday that markets for medium density fibreboard remained quite soft, especially in Asia.
"With new capacity coming on stream in 1997, both in New Zealand and other countries, worldwide operating rates will continue to be under pressure," CHH said.
The Forests and Wood Products group achieved EBIT of NZ$107 million in the nine months to December, against $163 million a year earlier.
Pulp, Paper and Tissue achieved EBIT of NZ$82 million compared to $140 million for the same period in 1995.
Pulp prices remained above the lows reached in the first quarter.
"The outlook for the near term will be difficult until worldwide inventory levels decline to more normal levels," CHH said.
Strong competition continued in all distribution and paper markets. Paper prices in the Australian market appeared to have stabilised after a turbulent 12 months.
"Both domestic and Australian markets have noted an improvement in activity levels in January," CHH said.
